title: Performance baseline record (CHE-105 / M0.4)
description: One measured workload. `environment` is what decides whether two of these may be compared at all; `workload.unit` and `workload.route` are what decide whether the comparison means anything, because cost per ray is a different quantity on an O(rays x pixels) route than on an O(rays) + FFT route.

size.description: How much work, in its natural unit. Never 'one run'.

route.description: Anything that changes the asymptotic cost model. Two records with the same unit and different routes are not comparable.

p95_s.description: NOT an interpolated percentile. The index is ceil(0.95n)-1, which is the slowest observed run for every n <= 19 and the second-slowest at n = 20. Read `tail_rule` rather than the field name: at the repeat counts this harness uses, a field called p95_s holds the max of 3.

tail_rule.description: How p95_s was actually obtained, machine-readable, so the rule travels with the number instead of living only in this schema.

gpu_count.description: Visible CUDA devices. AGENTS.md requires GPU measurements to be single-GPU; a count of 1 read from the runtime is what makes that checkable.

applied.description: False unless something actually pinned threads or affinity. Recording an affinity mask does not make a run isolated.

stages.description: Per-stage wall clock and each stage's share of the total. The share is the number CHE-101 needed: a 9.6x speedup on a stage worth 7% of the run moves the run by 7%.

fraction_of_total.description: Each stage's share of `total_s`, which is the elapsed time of the SAME call the stages were timed in -- not a median over repeats. A share above 1 is refused at write time rather than published.

total_s.description: The denominator of `fraction_of_total`: the elapsed seconds of the repeat whose stage timer this is. Present so a reader can check the shares rather than trust them.

cuda.description: This process's CUDA allocator state. `null` when the workload ran in a child process: a parent's snapshot is not the child's peak, and reporting the parent's zeros would read as 'the workload used no GPU memory'. For a whole-command baseline, the device memory is in the measured probe's own record.

swap_growth_bytes.description: Growth in the container cgroup's swap over the measurement. Nonzero means the run was aborted: swap as working memory is a stop condition, not a footnote. `null` means the cgroup file could not be read, which is reported rather than treated as zero.

subprocess.description: Present when the measured thing was a whole command rather than an in-process callable. The argv is part of the record because 'the test suite' is not a fixed workload -- it is whatever that command selects on the day.

returncode.description: Zero, always. A nonzero exit is refused by the runner rather than recorded: timing how long something took to crash and committing it as a baseline is worse than having no baseline.

peak_child_rss_bytes.description: Peak RSS of the measured child, from ru_maxrss over waited-for children. This is the workload's memory; the top-level `peak_host_rss_bytes` is the PARENT's and describes nothing about a whole-command baseline. `null` when the counter did not rise above the high-water mark left by an earlier child in this process.
